title: Depository Participant (DP) Charges & Debit Transaction Fees
content:
Official Depository Participant (DP) Charges for CDSL and NSDL Demat Accounts.

1. What is a DP Charge:
Depository Participant (DP) charge is an administrative fee collected by depositories (CDSL/NSDL) and the depository participant broker whenever shares are debited from an investor's demat account.

2. Pricing & Applicability:
- Rate: Flat Rs. 13.50 + 18% GST (total Rs. 15.93) per scrip (company) per day.
- Applicable on Selling: DP charges are levied strictly on delivery sell transactions. Buying shares incurs zero DP charges.
- Flat Per Scrip: The fee is charged per company per day, irrespective of the volume or value of shares sold. For example, whether you sell 1 share or 1,000 shares of Reliance Industries in a single day, the total DP charge debited is flat Rs. 13.50 + GST.
- Selling Multiple Scrips: If an investor sells shares of three different companies (e.g., TCS, Infosys, and HDFC Bank) on the same day, three separate DP charges apply (3 x Rs. 15.93 = Rs. 47.79).

3. Intra-day & Mutual Funds Exemption:
- Intraday equity trades do not involve shares moving in or out of the demat account, so intraday trades attract zero DP charges.
- Mutual funds redemptions and ETF unit creations follow separate scheme settlement schedules.

4. Pledge & Unpledge Transactions:
Pledge creation and pledge closure requests incur a fee of Rs. 20 + 18% GST per transaction per ISIN.
